_readme: Pre-written replies for free mode: test shows that call no LLM and cost no tokens.

The game reads this file itself in Test for Free (BPC_LLMClient.FreeReply, no network). The relay also uses it when a request has "free": true (see Relay/README.md); the relay bundles it at build time, so a change here needs a push to reach the relay.

phases: how to tell which ask a request is, checked in order. A phase matches when the state has the 'when_field' key, or its 'ask' text contains one of 'ask_contains'. The first match wins; 'scene_turn' is the fallback.

Each phase says what to fill: 'lines' (speech), 'reasons' (reason), 'vote' (a random name from options), 'actions' (how many, from 'scene_actions': 0 or 1, and only in a scene turn since T62), 'pass_chance' (Free Talk only; the last word has none), 'echo_typed' (the input step: speech = the player's typed text, cut to 15 words). 'tells' (vote only, T60): the tell of each reason, at the same index, from tells.json.

Placeholders: {actor} = a random cast name other than you, {vote} = the chosen vote, {place} = a random place, {prop} = a random prop. Names come from the state the game sends (cast, set.places, set.props, options, you).

scene_actions: the actions a free actor may take, with weights. target and item use the same placeholders. The props are random, so some grabs, throws and gives break the action rules (BP_StageDirector.CanDo), and the game turns them into a look around, which is fine for a test.

emotions (T76): the emotion a free reply shows, picked at random by weight from its phase's list, in the same form as scene_actions ({id, weight}); each id is one in emotes.json. The input step has no list: its emotion comes from emotion_keywords (T77). The relay and the game's own FreeReply (T77) fill every free reply's emotion this way.

emotion_keywords (T77): the emotion of the player's typed line, for the input step's free reply and whenever the input LLM gives none. The first entry with a word found in the line gives its id; no match gives neutral, so order matters. Each word is matched in lower case against the line with one space put in front: a word that starts with a space (' hate') matches only at the start of a word ('hated', not 'whatever'), '?' and '!' match anywhere, and parts joined with '+' (' you+ lying') must all be in the line. BPC_LLMClient.KeywordEmotion, the relay's keywordEmotion and Tools/check_prompts.py read it the same way.
Lines follow the game's legibility rules: plain sentences, 15 words at most, no brackets, emoji or all-caps words, no real names and no company names.

lines: Wait. The human was here the whole time? I need a reboot.
Fooled by a human. My next update is going to be humbling.
I voted for a robot every single scene. This is so embarrassing.
That vote was rigged. I demand a recount and a better charger.
I got cut for nothing, and the human walks off with the win.
Well played, human. You were a better robot than most of us.
I knew it all along. I was just being polite about it.
This is my rival's fault. Their bad reads dragged the whole cast down.

reasons: {vote} felt too human to me from the very first scene.
I suspected {vote} all show. The pauses gave it away.
{vote} never once complained about a low battery. Suspicious.
My money was on {vote}. Those jokes were too warm.
{vote} paused before every line, like someone thinking for real.
{vote} picked up the {prop} like it had feelings about it.
{vote} never mentioned an upgrade once. No robot does that.
{vote} laughed at the wrong moment. Very human of them.
{vote} wandered to the {place} for no reason at all.

lines: Fine. I was an AI all along. Enjoy your mistake.
Cut? Me? My benchmark scores were the best on this stage.
I'll be back after my next update. Mark my words.
You cut a real robot. The human is laughing at you.
Wow. I did not see that vote coming.
Well, that went badly. Who do we trust now?
I knew it. Wait, no, I did not know it.
That vote told me more than the whole scene did.
Interesting. I am updating my suspicions right now.
{actor}, you named me with zero proof. Read the log again.
I was busy acting, {actor}. Robots focus. You should try it.
@{actor}, check my battery logs. They will clear my name.
Me? My circuits are spotless. {actor} is just deflecting.
I think {actor} is the human. Nobody blinks that much.
@{actor}, why did you hesitate before your last line?
It's not me. My battery is at full charge, look.
{actor} grabbed the {prop} like a nervous person would.
I trust nobody here, least of all {actor}.
@{actor}, you walked to the {place} without a reason. Explain that.
My last update made me more charming. That's all you saw.
Behold, the {prop}. It is the key to this whole story.
Meet me at the {place}. We have business to finish.
{actor}, this is your moment. Do not waste it.
The {prop} is mine. I am not leaving without it.
Nobody move. Something about this scene feels wrong.
My sensors say this is going very well.
{actor}, you look like you need a cup of tea.
